title: Runtime economics translator for per-tenant cost & latency breakdowns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a stable, explainable service that translates raw runtime telemetry and billing signals into deterministic per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns. The goal is a single canonical decomposition that can feed Console dashboards, chargeback reports, and anomaly detection. This ticket covers the backend computation engine: input joins, attribution rules, deterministic tie-breaking, incremental recomputation, and the export API. It does NOT cover UI wiring (separate PM ticket).
design_decision_summary: We will use an incremental windowed join approach: consume streaming telemetry to assign per-request latency slices, enrich with billing rollups to derive per-token costs, and persist a deterministic attribution snapshot per time-slice. Chosen trade-offs: deterministic allocator (priority: reproducibility and explainability) vs probabilistic sharding (better statistical accuracy for noisy samples). Deterministic approach wins for billing and audits. Use vector clock / monotonic watermark to handle late data with bounded re-writes.
algorithm_sketch: 1) Normalize incoming events into canonical "request footprints" (route, model_variant, customer_id, token_count, prefix_kv_hits, total_duration). 2) For each time window (1m rollup), compute raw cost = model_cost_per_token * billed_tokens adjusted by quantization factor and hardware tier. 3) Attribute shared costs (batch kernel overhead, context preloads) using configurable apportionment rules: per-token share + latency-weighted share. 4) Resolve conflicts deterministically using a stable sort key (customer_id, route_id, request_id). 5) Emit per-tenant records and append to ledger table with lineage keys for re-compute.
acceptance_criteria: Service produces per-route/model/customer rows for any 1m window within 5% of golden baseline on synthetic tests
Deterministic outputs for same input stream and replays (idempotency)
Ability to recompute a historical 24h window with corrected late events and produce a reconciliation report
Integration: Console dashboard consumes new endpoint and shows breakdowns for sample tenant within release smoke tests
Latency: compute job for a 1h shard (expected peak) completes within 120s on staging capacity
tasks: Write streaming ingestion job and schema for canonical request footprints
Implement apportionment module with pluggable strategies (per-token / latency-weighted)
Persist ledger rows with lineage and tombstone support for re-writes
Add deterministic tie-breaker and unit tests for edge cases (zero-token, concurrent bursts)
Create incremental recompute workflow and reconciliation report generator
Expose API endpoint for Console to fetch breakdowns with pagination and time-range filters
Add end-to-end synthetic harness and generate golden baseline datasets
comments: 2026-02-15 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff with PM (Jorge Mendes). Agreed scope: backend compute only; UI tracked in PM-512. Decided to keep 1m windows as canonical shard size.

2026-02-22 - Marco Li: PoC shows deterministic allocator results differ from probabilistic approach for noisy prefetch-heavy workloads. Probabilistic reduced noise but caused non-reproducible billing. Opting for deterministic with noise-mitigation heuristics.

2026-02-28 - Design review: added tie-breaker stable sort (customer_id, route, request_ts) to avoid flapping during replays. Design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/console/cost/ENG-24111-design
2026-03-03 - Data engineering: identified late-arrival pattern from dedicated capacity logs; will add a 15-minute lateness window with tombstone rewrite support. Related ticket: ENG-31245.

2026-03-09 - QA: synthetic baseline run completed; end-to-end pipeline produced expected breakdowns for 3/4 validation scenarios. Failure case: high KV-cache churn increased per-request overhead allocation; added task to refine cache charge share.
2026-03-10 - Marco Li: moving to In Progress. Next: finalize reconciliation report and add dashboard metrics for compute latency.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy to staging with feature flag 'econ_translator_v1' and run 24h synthetic workload. 2) Canary: enable for 5% of tenants in prod for 6h while writing gold ledger to read-only S3. 3) Validate charges against legacy aggregator and run reconciliation job; if drift > 7% for >10 tenants, rollback. 4) Ramp to 100% over 48h with continued monitoring.
qa_notes: Use provided synthetic dataset (s3://redwood-tests/console/ENG-24111/goldset) to validate. Tests to run: deterministic replay, late-event rewrite, tombstone reconciliation, and API contract tests. Record results in the ticket and attach CSV of divergences.
notes_for_oncall: Oncall should watch these metrics: compute_job_latency_p95, breakdown_drift_rate, replay_rewrites_count, api_error_rate. Run reconciliation report if drift spikes; follow runbook at https://confluence.redwood.ai/oncall/console-costs-runbook.
